messages:
dina: Quick UX/accessible flow question: for 'Force approve' on mixed bundles we want an inline justification step. Current mock opens a modal with a textarea but keyboard flow feels clunky. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/force-21688.png

samir: thanks. What's the clunkiest part? focus order, required field validation, or modal close?

dina: focus lands on textarea (good) but after typing, pressing Enter from keyboard submits unexpectedly because primary is also triggered. We should make Enter insert newline in textarea and use Ctrl+Enter or the primary button to submit.

ava: agree. Textareas should accept Enter; primary should be triggered by Ctrl+Enter or Meta+Enter for power users. Also add a visible helper: "Submit with Ctrl+Enter" and put it under the textarea.

leah: microcopy debate: label above textarea: options: (A) "Reason for forcing approval (required)" (B) "Justification (required, will be logged)" (C) "Explain why these failing tests should be approved" Thoughts?

samir: I like B 1 it's concise and mentions logging which is important for auditing.

designbot: Accessibility check: modal needs role="dialog" and aria-modal="true". Ensure textarea has aria-required="true" and aria-describedby pointing to helper text. Contrast for helper link is 3.9:1 borderline; recommend darker token.

dina: what about default focus after submit? Should we return to the bundle anchor and show a toast that includes an undo link?

ava: yes. Return focus to the approve anchor and open a non-blocking toast with "Force-approved N tests" and an "Undo" action. Focus stays in the page; press Esc while toast focused should dismiss it. Also include the audit entry ID in the toast for quick access.

leah: implementation note: when we do force-approve require at least 20 characters in the textarea to avoid perfunctory approvals. Is 20 too strict?

samir: 20 seems fine as a soft guard; validate client-side and show hint "Please provide more detail (min 20 characters)" with polite aria-live updates.

designbot: Contrast advisory: danger button on modal primary (red-500) over white has 4.2:1 1 passes AA for 14pt but borderline for 12pt. Consider bold label or darker red-600.

dina: also, keyboard help: when modal opens, pressing Tab should move: close icon -> textarea -> helper -> submit -> cancel. Shift+Tab cycles backward. After submit, focus returns to approve anchor.

ava: can we add an optional check-box "Affects historical data" that when checked reveals a secondary confirmation requiring typing the bundle name to confirm? For high-risk force-approves only.

samir: yes conditionally showing a second confirm step is fine. If checkbox checked, show "Type bundle name to confirm" input; require exact match. That input needs aria-label and a semantic description of which historical artifacts will change.

dina: final microcopy for primary: "Force approve N tests" secondary: "Cancel" danger confirm title: "Force approve and modify history?" body: "This operation will change historical scorecards. Type the bundle name to confirm."

leah: I'll update Figma frames with these interactions and the keyboard hints. Will also try darker tokens and wire the aria-describedby IDs.

ava: perfect 1 let's review tomorrow in sync. If anyone wants different wording for the undo toast or confirmation blurbs drop them here before 9am. :memo:
